name: Enforce and verify transport encryption across all information paths
description: Set a transport standard, enforce it centrally at boundary components, and verify what deployed endpoints actually negotiate rather than trusting the configuration.

steps.action: Enumerate every endpoint that terminates or originates protected information traffic, including APIs, webhooks, outbound integrations, and internal service-to-service paths.
Set a minimum protocol version and cipher suite list in the cryptography policy, and record the basis for the choice.
Enforce the standard at the load balancer, ingress controller, or service mesh so clients inherit it rather than configuring it individually.
Refuse plaintext connections rather than redirecting them, where the client population allows it.
Run recurring independent validation against every enumerated endpoint and retain the dated output.
Alert on validation failures so a deployment that weakens transport is detected rather than discovered at audit.

implementation_considerations: Raising the minimum protocol version can break older client integrations. Identify affected customers and sequence the change with notice rather than enforcing unilaterally.
Refusing rather than redirecting plaintext is the more defensible position but produces opaque failures for misconfigured clients; weigh support cost.
Internal service-to-service traffic is often the largest omission and the hardest to retrofit; treat it as its own workstream.
Set the standard at a level the estate can actually meet. A policy naming a version legacy integrations cannot support manufactures its own exceptions.
typical_duration: Weeks for external endpoints; internal service mesh adoption is typically longer.
prerequisites: An inventory of endpoints carrying protected information
Agreement on the minimum standard, including its impact on existing clients

verification_method.how: Run independent validation against every enumerated endpoint and confirm each negotiates at or above the documented standard, and that plaintext is handled as the policy states.

residual_risk_note: Endpoints created after validation runs are unverified until the next cycle. Continuous validation narrows but does not close that window.
period_limitation_note: Strengthening transport configuration now does not change what endpoints negotiated during an elapsed period.
notes: DriftGuard recommends a standard aligned to current industry guidance but does not assert a required protocol version, because SOC 2 names none.
